help.title: Help
help.keys:
↑/↓      select a call (or a unit after Tab)
Tab      switch between the call queue and the unit list
1–9      pick / unpick units to send (several are allowed)
Enter    send the picked units to the selected call
Esc      clear the picked units
D        dismiss the selected call (pranks, non-emergencies)
F        flag the selected call as suspicious for Inspector Dilshod
R        recall the unit under the cursor, or every unit of the selected call
C        coffee break, once per shift: no new calls for 15 min, less stress, a little less trust
Space    pause / resume            +/−   speed ×1 ×2 ×4
L        language: O'zbekcha / Русский / English
?        this help                 Q     quit (asks first)
help.legend:
Map: ! a call (yellow → red = severity, white = selected), ⚑ a flagged call, digits = units on the move
     H hospital, F fire station, P police, + railway ambulance post, ║ bridge, × flooded bridge
Units: A ambulance (green), F fire engine (red), P patrol car (cyan); ~N = minutes to the selected call
Severity: ! minor, !! serious, !!! critical — a critical call is lost if nobody arrives in time

cli.usage:
Dispatch 112 — a real-time emergency-dispatch simulator for the terminal

Usage: dispatch112 [options]

  --lang uz|ru|en          interface language
  --difficulty rookie|dispatcher|veteran
  --seed N                 fixed random seed for a new game
  --autoplay               the bot plays inside the TUI (demo)
  --headless               play one week with the bot, no TUI, print a summary
  --seeds N                with --headless: run seeds 1..N and print a balance table
  --bot good|noflags|sloppy|idle   bot profile for --headless
  --help, --version

Progress is saved between shifts in ~/.dispatch112/progress.json (set DISPATCH112_HOME to change).
cli.try_help: Run with --help to see the options.
